### Changelogs:

Remove version constraint of httpx

#### [0.3.1](https://github.com/home-assistant-ecosystem/python-glances-api/releases/tag/0.3.1)
Add exception for invalid credentials (Thanks @engrbm87)

#### [0.3.0](https://github.com/home-assistant-ecosystem/python-glances-api/releases/tag/0.3.0)
Migrate to pyproject style
Mgrate to httpx

#### [0.2.1](https://github.com/home-assistant-ecosystem/python-glances-api/releases/tag/0.2.1)
Only allow aiohttp >= 3.7.4 to avoid CVE-2021-21330

I'm not 100% sure.
It seems that it's used to get the clientSession via `async_get_clientsession`
which later on was passed to [Glances](https://github.com/home-assistant-ecosystem/python-glances-api) (in order to be used as the context of the calls)

This change is in this commit:

What happens if a user connects to a server with ssl option set to True, ie to a https server endpoint, and the server has an invalid certificate?

~`ssl` is still part of the API, so why remove the option?~
~https://github.com/home-assistant-ecosystem/python-glances-api/blob/e3c7e281196a44f74c20dab2ddf9b10a38623acb/glances_api/__init__.py#L16-L26~
Edit: I can't read and distinguish `ssl` versus `verify_ssl`

~Maybe it should simply be passed to the API now, instead of completely dropped.~
Edit: I can't read and distinguish `ssl` versus `verify_ssl`

> What happens if a user connects to a server with ssl option set to True, ie to a https server endpoint, and the server has an invalid certificate?

Basically - what you're asking is the following:
1. Does `httpx` client do the certificate validation out-of-the-box by default or not?
2. Do we want to allow the user to override this behavior?

To answer the first part - copying from https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/#changing-the-verification-defaults:

Or you can also disable the SSL verification entirely, which is not recommended.
...
```
client = httpx.Client(verify=False)
```

So probably the answer is Yes.

Question 2 remains open (I'm afraid to decide on this one)


We could, ideally - pass the `validate_ssl` parameter to `Glances` and decide either we want to use it there - not breaking any functionality, but this would require changes in `Glances` (API) code

Something like this:
https://github.com/home-assistant-ecosystem/python-glances-api/pull/4

> I think we should update the library to accept an optional httpx client. The home assistant httpx client already has an option for verify ssl.
> 
> I think we should not merge this until we do this to avoid a breaking change.
